minutes.headline: Select Board approved two restaurants' outdoor seating, recommended passing over some articles, and heard debate on streetlight purchase.
minutes.summary: The Select Board met remotely before the June 13 Town Meeting. It approved outdoor seating and alcohol service applications for two restaurants with a signed compliance letter, voted on deferred articles, and met jointly with the Finance Committee on a consent calendar and the streetlight LED purchase. Members also discussed racial-disparity outreach with other towns, the town manager's report, and public comments on cemeteries and Town Meeting check-in.

public_comment.topic: A member read a statement urging that spending articles (capital plan, streetlights, earth removal) be moved to a November Town Meeting for safety and fiscal caution.
Cemetery Commission chairman criticised the condition of town cemeteries over Memorial Day weekend and said the commission has no control over maintenance.
A member asked that the streetlight LED article and the capital plan be passed over to November because of cost and lack of public engagement.
A resident complained that the 8:00 check-in time for Town Meeting was not well advertised.
Resident praised the weekend protest and asked for attention to speeding and child safety on streets this summer.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved outdoor seating and alcohol service applications for On the Rocks and Embers, on condition each signs a compliance letter within one week.
The Select Board voted to recommend passing over Articles 4 and 9, the latter a sewer budget adjustment, ahead of the June 13 Town Meeting.
A motion to recommend the earth removal article (22) was withdrawn, and Articles 22 and 24 were left deferred.
Meeting jointly, the Finance Committee and Select Board agreed a consent calendar and kept eleven contested articles off it, including 22 and 24.
On the streetlight LED purchase there was no resolution; the motion sheet is to be changed to a higher amount rather than amended at Town Meeting.

why_it_matters: The streetlight purchase would draw on free cash, and members discussed whether that reduces the free cash available for the stabilization deposit, so the outcome touches the town's reserves and future tax pressure.
Articles left off the consent calendar will each be debated and voted separately at Town Meeting, so residents who care about them need to attend and check in on time.
watch_next: Town Meeting on June 13, where the streetlight article and the contested articles come to a vote.
The town manager's answer on the funding source for Green Communities grants, due before Thursday.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the two main Select Board votes (restaurant applications, passing over Article 4) and on Article 24 staying deferred. They differ on the votes on Articles 9, 22 and 14, and on the CARES Act figure, which is cut off in the official text.
